## Overall Summary
This work addresses the challenge of long-horizon robotic assembly, which requires coupling high-level semantic reasoning with low-level geometric constraints. Pure semantic planners often lack physical grounding, leading to logical brittleness, while native geometric solvers suffer from combinatorial explosion in complex tasks. The authors propose VLM-LGP, a hierarchical framework that integrates Vision-Language Models for logical skeleton extraction with a deterministic Branch-Aware Topological Clustering algorithm to prune the search space. This system guides Logic-Geometric Programming solvers to ensure both semantic coherence and kinematic feasibility. Key contributions include the introduction of a Layered Precedence Graph for temporal ordering, shape-aware manipulation primitives for diverse objects, and a visual-semantic validator for safety halting. The framework aims to overcome the limitations of Task and Motion Planning by reducing manual specification requirements and handling closed kinematic loops through topological decoupling.

## Complete Method Description
The VLM-LGP framework operates as a hierarchical planning system designed to bridge the gap between discrete symbolic logic and continuous trajectory optimization. The process initiates with scene initialization and reachability pre-checks to establish a robust physical foundation before semantic reasoning occurs. A standard Vision module recognizes object shapes and confirms their six-degree-of-freedom poses, mapping them to physical proxies within the simulation environment. Objects are spatially sorted based on radial Euclidean distance from the robot base to establish a preliminary reasoning sequence. Concurrently, a Reachability Pre-check invokes a Layer-1 Logic-Geometric Programming solver to test basic grasp feasibility under global collision constraints. This low-cost pre-filter evaluates whether a valid waypoint exists for each object within a maximum time threshold, categorizing objects as reachable or unreachable. By eliminating kinematically impossible candidates early, the system prevents costly downstream failures during full-motion solving.

Following initialization, the system extracts a Layered Precedence Graph to define the temporal skeleton of the assembly task. A Vision-Language Model acts as a high-level zero-shot parser to process visual assembly instructions, generating an ordered sequence of semantic placement tasks. Each node in this graph encapsulates a disjoint assembly stage, such as placing a foundation before a second layer, while directed edges encode physical support dependencies. This graph serves as an abstract temporal structure where upstream nodes must be fully completed before downstream actions commence. A Python compliance monitor continuously validates execution strategies against this graph, immediately rejecting any downstream strategy that violates the topological ordering. This ensures that the semantic reasoning remains physically grounded throughout the planning horizon.

To manage the combinatorial explosion of the search space, the framework employs a dynamic pruning pipeline comprising a Semantic Resource Allocator and a Logic Batch Compiler. The allocator binds generic object requests to uniquely available physical entities in the simulation inventory. Strategy generation is then handled by a deterministic Branch-Aware Topological Clustering algorithm rather than stochastic evaluation. This algorithm computes a topological depth for each object to ensure strict placement ordering based on support dependencies. The structure is spatially partitioned into branches, such as left versus right structural pillars, through recursive propagation of support dependencies. Objects spanning multiple branches are identified as bridges to serve as synchronization points. Based on these computed layers and branches, placeable objects are grouped into executable, collision-free batches. This guarantees physical stability and exposes parallel execution roots. The Logic Batch Compiler subsequently translates the selected sub-graph into hardware-safe execution batches, outputting flat, atomic facts adhering to native Logic-Geometric Programming syntax.

The geometric execution phase translates these logic bounds into continuous trajectory optimization using a k-order Markov Optimization solver. To resolve local geometric feasibility, the core action skeleton is refined through specialized manipulation primitives. For box-type objects, the grasp constrains the gripper to be centered on the target frame in the XY plane while leaving the Z axis free for optimization, guided by a pre-grasp funnel. For cylindrical objects, the primitive enforces strict orthogonality between the gripper approach axis and the cylinder central axis while permitting translational sliding along the length. This formulation grants the solver maximal freedom to determine the optimal grasp height, which is critical for collision-free manipulation in dense scenes. Additionally, to handle multi-support structural scenarios that violate strict tree topology assumptions, the system introduces a virtual anchor parented to the world frame. This anchor allows the solver to break closed kinematic loops by locking the anchor to a target pose and employing soft alignment to guide the object, enabling dynamic interpolation of the most stable geometric descent.

Safety and robustness are maintained through an Active Constraint Strategy and a Visual-Semantic Validator. The Active Constraint Strategy interleaves dynamic constraint activation between waypoint generation and full-motion optimization. Collision pairs are selectively activated based on geometric proximity within a dynamic spatial radius, ignoring irrelevant scene objects to shrink the search manifold. If a solve fails, the radius expands for a principled fallback. Finally, after each executed batch, the Visual-Semantic Validator captures top-down visual observations to detect geometric deviations against the expected blueprint state. If errors such as missing components or intruder objects are detected, the system halts the planning pipeline to prevent cascading structural failures.
